issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Lecture.addGuestStudents: The template declares Lecture.addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) (template expects two parameters), while the problem statement (task description and UML) specifies addGuestStudents(int) returning void, and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (one int parameter). This inconsistency will cause compilation or test mismatches and confuse students about the expected signature and how they should implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template signature match the problem statement and solution: change the template method to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } and remove the extra boolean parameter. Implement the method to add the given number to numberOfGuestStudents. Alternatively, if an input-validation boolean was intended, update the problem statement and solution to document and implement the two-parameter version consistently.

issues.description: Method signing mismatch for the 'addGuestStudents' concept: the problem statement explicitly requires a method addGuestStudents(int) (problem calls it addGuestStudents with a single int parameter). The template implementation declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) (an extra boolean parameter), while the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (single int parameter). Students following the task and tests will expect the single-parameter signature; the extra boolean in the template prevents a direct mapping and may break tests or confuse students about the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution. Change the template declaration from public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and implement the addition logic (or perform any validation internally without changing the signature) so the template, problem description, and solution share the same method name and parameter list.
